A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the IQA-Adapter research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Retained content can be matched across the substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original SDXL experiments, benchmark evaluations, sensitivity analyses, and a subjective study involving 1,017 participants.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds reference-based distortion-transfer experiments, architectural ablations, external baseline comparisons, and timing measurements.

M1.justification: V2 Sections 3.3–3.4 introduce Reference-based IQA-Adapter, which conditions generation on intermediate ARNIQA embeddings extracted from reference images and uses degradation augmentation during training. This substantially extends the score-based conditioning procedure in v1. The original attention mechanism and denoising objective remain; renaming the attention mechanism does not itself change the method.

E1.justification: V2 adds direct KADID-10k evaluation of reference-conditioned distortion transfer in both SDEdit image editing and text-to-image generation (Section 4.5). These introduce reference images and distortion-reproduction requirements beyond v1's score-controlled generation. KADID previously appeared as training data for pretrained IQA models. Lexica.art, PartiPrompts, GenEval, and COCO coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V2 evaluates DiffusionDPO, Q-Refine, BeautifulPrompt, and Prompt Weighting against IQA-Adapter in quality, GenEval, and COCO comparisons, including several combinations with the adapter. The new distortion-transfer comparison adds IP-Adapter and, for text-to-image generation, StyleCrafter (Table 2). V1's comparisons primarily involved the base model, gradient guidance, and IQA-Adapter variants.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a distortion-transfer protocol using one reference source, 80 target images, and 125 distortion variants, evaluated through quality correlations, CLIP comparisons, and ARNIQA embedding similarity. It also adds HPSv2 scoring, architectural control configurations, and a controlled runtime evaluation. The original training schedule and basic SDXL sampling settings are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct ablation of separate qualitative attention against concatenating quality and text tokens, with quantitative and visual evidence (Table 5, Figure 16). It also adds computational-overhead analysis and reference-transfer failure comparisons. V1's positional-encoding, adapter-scale, seed-consistency, and GradCAM analyses are largely retained and reorganized, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 Section 17.1 and Table 8 newly report timing averages over 1,000 generations with ± values, although the meaning of those spreads is unspecified. The original 25-prompt, 100-seed analysis, subjective-study counts, and Inception Score uncertainty-reporting practice remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial distortion-transfer, baseline, combination, ablation, and runtime results. Retained COCO values are also revised: base-model FID changes from 21.84 to 19.92, and TOPIQ+LAION-AES FID from 23.51 to 21.36 (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 7). These are reported-value revisions without an explanation establishing an algorithmic gain. The original main GenEval table and subjective-study results are retained.

T1.justification: The negative-condition definition is generalized from qneg = -q in v1 Section 8 to qneg = -δq in v2 Section 3.2.1, introducing a tunable quality gap. The attention equations, denoising objective, relative-gain definition, and positional-encoding formula otherwise retain their mathematical content. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion elevate learning from internal IQA activations and content-agnostic reference-image quality transfer to central contributions. V1 centers on score-conditioned generation and its degradation and adversarial applications. The claims of up to 10% quality improvement and preservation of generative capabilities are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations concerning semantic leakage from reference images, the suitability of IQA embeddings for distortion transfer, attention separation, and compatibility with other improvement methods. Its limitations discussion adds artifact-classifier and latent-space assessment directions, while Section 18 extends the adversarial-risk discussion to critic-based optimization. Most earlier IQA-bias and VAE limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 Section 9 newly discloses per-GPU batch sizes of 16 and 4, training on five nodes with 40 GPUs, and reference-adapter and negative-guidance settings. The timing experiment specifies hardware, precision, resolution, and sampling steps. These improve documentation; the newly disclosed batch sizes do not establish changed training. The promised code and weights release remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantive Generation Quality Improvement discussion positioning IQA-Adapter against DiffusionDPO, Q-Refine, prompt enhancement, and other quality-improvement approaches. It also situates reference conditioning relative to IP-Adapter and StyleCrafter, with additional citations supporting the new experiments. The distinction between broad quality control and quality maximization becomes more explicit.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related work are substantially rewritten. Discussion moves from the main paper into the supplement, while negative guidance moves into the main method description. The supplement gains a contents section and reorganizes limitations, ablations, and additional experiments. These are extensive narrative and structural changes beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 2 to include embedding-based conditioning and reorganizes comparison heatmaps with colored method categories. It adds distortion-transfer, ablation, and runtime tables, expands existing comparison tables, and introduces several qualitative comparison grids. Existing figures are relocated, while the earlier negative-guidance displays are reduced or replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important evidential gaps in v1 through external quality-improvement baselines and a direct architectural ablation, substantially strengthening assessment of the method's usefulness and design choices. The reference-based extension receives quantitative and visual evaluation, and training disclosure improves. Unexplained revisions to retained scores and the Table 5 versus Section 11.1 SROCC mismatch remain reporting weaknesses; the improvement rests on stronger comparisons and controls, rather than higher reported numbers.
